title: Operator Curation Hub & Mini-Saga Runner: lightweight curated runbook assembly for quick remediations
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: First-line responders and SREs frequently need small, multi-step remediations composed from existing runbook fragments (e.g., rotate a host, restart a service, and surface relevant logs). Today those workflows are ad-hoc: typed into Slack, executed manually, or baked into heavyweight playbooks that are slow to maintain.

Objective: Build an Operator Curation Hub (OCH) + Mini-Saga Runner: a lightweight service that lets operators surface, compose, validate, and execute short idempotent remediation sequences (mini-sagas) made from curated runbook fragments. The system should support dry-run, approval gating, telemetry, and safe rollbacks. It must integrate with existing runbook fragments repo, the admin console, and the telemetry/alerting stack.

Scope & non-goals:
- In-scope: fragment registry, composition UI/API, deterministic executor, dry-run harness, permission checks, telemetry events, PR/approval flow integration.
- Out-of-scope: full authoring experience for long-form runbooks, complex cross-account orchestration, or replacing the existing long-running orchestration engine.

Design highlights & trade-offs:
1) Composition model: fragments are typed (check, mutate, notify). We will implement a small DSL (YAML-based) to declare inputs, outputs, and compensation actions. Trade-off: DSL reduces flexibility vs a full scripting layer but increases safety and verifiability.
2) Execution semantics: Mini-sagas run with at-least-once attempts and strict idempotency keys; a compensating action is required for any mutating fragment. Trade-off: stronger guarantees require more metadata and author discipline.
3) Storage: fragment metadata stored in an internal Postgres table; artifacts (scripts) referenced by SHA and stored in the runbook artifact store (S3). This keeps service lightweight and allows reuse.
4) Safety: every mutating composition must be flagged and either require an approval or run on a restricted agent pool. We will reuse RBAC policies from admin-console-iam to gate execution.

Acceptance criteria:
- Create fragment registry API (CRUD) and UI surface in console for curators.
- Composer UI that lets operator select fragments, view composed plan, and run dry-run producing simulated telemetry.
- Executor that runs mini-sagas with idempotency, logs per-step telemetry, and emits structured audit events to the audit pipeline.
- Integration tests demonstrating dry-run vs real-run parity for 5 representative fragments (restart service, rotate key, collect heapdump, update route, drain instance).
- Security review sign-off and SSO/RBAC integration.

Milestones & rollout plan:
- Week 1 (MVP): Fragment registry, CLI/API, basic composer (console stub), basic executor with dry-run (no mutates allowed in dry-run), unit tests.
- Week 2: Mutating steps enabled behind feature flag, RBAC gating, per-step compensations required, telemetry hooks.
- Week 3: Add approvals flow, PR-based fragment onboarding, canary rollout to internal SRE team.
- Week 4: Expand to firstline support with training docs, incident-runbook pairing, and SLA for page-to-remediate time.

Integration points / links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Ops/Operator+Curation+Hub+PRD
- Proto UI mocks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1OCH-UI-MOCKS
- Prototype executor repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/mini-saga-runner/pull/42
- Telemetry spec: https://docs.redwood.ai/telemetry/mini-saga-events

Implementation notes for engs:
- API design: /api/v1/fragments, /api/v1/compositions, /api/v1/executions
- Execution model: worker pool subscribes over EventBridge; lightweight steps executed in isolated ephemeral sandboxes (gVisor) for safety.
- Idempotency: execution_id + step_id + resource_token used to detect replays.
- Compensation enforcement: each mutating fragment must declare compensating_fragment_id; executor will abort composition if missing.
- Testing: include a sandbox-run harness that can replay recorded traces from incident playbacks.

Potential blockers:
- RBAC mapping for transient operator roles (need IAM schema tweak, ENG-772005).
- Existing fragment artifact format alignment (depends on ENG-314159 artifact normalization).
- Approval UX complexity (coord with PM and Design).

Notes on metrics to surface:
- median step latency, success rate per fragment, aborted compositions, dry-run vs real-run delta, manual overrides count, audit-event delivery lag.

- Spike: build a one-step prototype that can rotate an ephemeral key in the sandbox (owner: Lia Nguyen, ETA 2026-03-05).
- Security kickoff for review (owner: Priya Rao, due 2026-03-10).
